chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who divorces his wife before consummating the marriage. He said: 'If he divorces her before consummating the marriage, she is separated from him, and she may marry whomever she wishes immediately.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorce before consummation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that in the case of divorce before consummation, the separation is immediate and absolute, granting the wife full freedom to remarry without the obligation of observing the three-month waiting period (iddah al-talaq) prescribed for those who have been married. This ruling is derived from the specific linguistic structure of the Quranic verse, distinguishing it from the general divorce process, and underscores the juristic consensus in Shia fiqh regarding the efficacy of the pronouncement even prior to physical intimacy.
